memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the officers shall add, "Is anyone afraid or fainthearted? Let him go home so that his fellow soldiers will not become disheartened too." When the officers have finished speaking to the army, they shall appoint commanders over it. - Deut 20:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's instructions include another release, anyone who was truly afraid and fainthearted could go home. Why? Because fear is contagious. One trembling soldier could spread discouragement through the whole army. God allowed those overwhelmed by fear to step back rather than infect others with dread.

There is honesty here about the reality of fear. God does not shame the fearful man or force him into a battle his heart cannot face. Yet He also protects the community from the spread of that fear. Both the individual and the group are cared for.

There is wisdom for us in this. Fear and discouragement can spread from person to person, and our attitudes affect those around us. This calls us to be careful about the spirit we carry into our families, churches, and workplaces. Do we spread faith and courage, or fear and complaint? At the same time, God is gentle with the fearful. He does not despise a trembling heart. Instead, He invites us to bring our fears to Him and be strengthened. Perfect love, His love, drives out fear (1 John 4:18). As we grow closer to Christ, our fear gives way to trust. Are you spreading courage or discouragement to those around you, and are you bringing your own fears honestly to God?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you spread courage or discouragement to others?
2. How honestly do you bring your fears to God?
3. Where do you need His perfect love to drive out fear?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me carry courage and faith to those around me. Thank You for being gentle with my fears, drawing me into Your perfect love. Amen.
